result.topic_en: Gauss works out the counts a, b, c, d of Gaussian integers of given residue classes modulo 1+i in the four triangles of a square (lattice-point counts related to biquadratic residues), tabulates these counts for many complex primes p = A+Bi, and describes a counting method for determining a-d.

[diagram: square divided by its diagonals into four triangles labelled $c$ (top), $d$ (left), $b$ (right), $a$ (bottom); corners labelled $ip$ (lower left) and $0$ (lower right)]

$a = b+c \equiv 0 (\mathrm{mod}\ 1+i)$
$=(a+d) \equiv 0 (\mathrm{mod}\ 2)$
$+(b+c) \equiv i (\mathrm{mod}\ 2)$
$b = a+d \equiv 0 (\mathrm{mod}\ 1+i)$
$=(b+c) \equiv 0\ \mathrm{mod}\ 2$
$+(a+d) \equiv 1\ \mathrm{mod}\ 2$
$c = b+c \equiv 1 (\mathrm{mod}\ 1+i)$
$=(b+c) \equiv 1 (\mathrm{mod}\ 2)$
$+(a+d) \equiv 1+i (\mathrm{mod}\ 2)$
$d = a+d \equiv 1 (\mathrm{mod}\ 1+i)$
$=(a+d) \equiv i (\mathrm{mod}\ 2)$
$+(b+c) \equiv 1+i\ \mathrm{mod}\ 2$

Hieraus $a = b$
$= \frac{1}{2}(a+b+c+d) \equiv 0 (\mathrm{mod}\ 1+i)$

Zur Bestimmung von $a-d$
Es sei $\alpha$, {+$\delta$+} die Anzahl der durch $1+i$ theilbaren Zahlen
in den [-Raum-] Parallelogrammen
$\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 0+\frac{1}{2}i \ldots \frac{1}{2}(A+Bi)+\frac{1}{2}i \\ \frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}i \ldots \frac{1}{2}(A+Bi)+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}i \end{array} \right\}$
$\left\{ \begin{array}{l} \frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}i \quad \frac{1}{2}(A+Bi)+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}i \\ 1+\frac{1}{2}i \quad \frac{1}{2}(A+Bi)+1+\frac{1}{2}i \end{array} \right\}$
Dann ist $a-d = \alpha-\delta$
Durch Rechnung so: Es bedeute $t$ die Zahlen $1, 2, 3, \ldots \frac{1}{2}B$
Zähle die [-ganzen-] Zahlen zwischen $2at-a$ und $2at+b-a$
die durch $2b$ theilbar sind, zu $\alpha$ insofern der Quotient mit $t$
zugleich gerade oder ungerade ist; eben so die zwischen
$2at+b-a$ und $2at+2b-a$ zu $\delta$.
Z. B. $13+4i$
$t$ | Grenzen | Divisor = 8 | Quotient | Also $\alpha-\delta=0$
1 | 13 17 21 | | 2 auszuschl.
2 | 39 43 47 | | 5 [-gerade-]

methods.what: Congruence conditions mod 1+i and mod 2 defining the four triangle regions a, b, c, d of the square on p
Derived relation that counts a and b are equal and half the total is divisible by 1+i
Table of counts a.b.c.d for Gaussian primes A+Bi with B = 2,...,14
Reduction of a-d to difference of counts of numbers divisible by 1+i in two parallelograms
Counting algorithm for alpha and delta via integers divisible by 2b in intervals with parity condition on quotient and t
